title: A Monarch Divided As He Seems To Mend

contact_edits.before: One last subtlety:When Lear at the end says "and my poor fool is hanged," audiences have always taken for granted that he means the Fool, while the unsentimental insist that he means Cordelia. Bedford has it both ways. His Lear is confused; he thinks that he means the Fool, then you can see him jerked back to reality as he remembers that the actual victim, there dead beside him, is someone ever more precious. "Break heart, I prithee break" says Kent; and it does. So, I think, will yours. - King Lear is in repertory at the Stratford Festival until Oct. 28. For tickets, call 1-800-567-1600 or visit www.stratfordfestival.ca
